plan.grounded.why: Most of what the plan says traces to the brief. That includes Reuben's left curve and giant left testicle, the dishwasher-safe tattoo, both hook/truth pairs, the drawer items (collarbone clip, £240 harness, lentils, mirror rehearsals) and both clinician fears. It notices the two characters' mirrored drawers: both have posture gadgets, both rehearse in the mirror, and both use a 'just got in/back' lie. It stays at 4 because core material is left out: Reuben's band name-drop test, which is how 'the door actually opens', plus his arm wrestling and Brick's wrong-correct-address habit and monocle-in-rosé.
evidence: trading their two posture contraptions and skipping the mirror rehearsal
Brick's revolving-door heel (planted as "architectural incompetence"
plan.grounded.raise: Build one of Reuben's tests around his band-era name-drop, and give Brick a way to pass or fail it.

plan.contradictions.why: The plan puts Brick 'standing at her counter in a towel since four'. In the brief she was 'on the sofa since four, in the same towel', and the rosé was finished at the counter 'reading old messages', so two drawer facts are fused into one scene that breaks both. Reuben's firing changes 'misidentified as someone famous' into mistaking a regular for 'an indie singer's brother', and the brother isn't the famous one. The plan also writes 'Massive length' without noticing the brief's trap, where Brick's backstory says her tip 'finishes shorter than the eye expects'.
evidence: Drank three-liter boxed rosé standing at her counter in a towel since four
fired for lecturing a regular he mistook for an indie singer's brother
plan.contradictions.raise: Keep the towel on the sofa and the rosé at the counter as separate facts, and reconcile or flag Brick's tip-length conflict.

plan.evaluation.why: The plan has fears and snaps but never states what each character needs. Reuben's need, 'stays present through pauses, engages your real interests', is only implied by his snap at 'a pause'. Brick's need, someone 'patient, exact, consistent', is not addressed. The tests are implicit, and it is never said what Reuben offers that answers Brick's fear of being too big, or what Brick offers that answers his fear of being negligible. The click outcomes show the guard dropping but not why.
evidence: A pause or feeling measured makes him formally declare the match dead on arrival
Feeling mocked as "too much" triggers a cold numbered ruling
plan.evaluation.raise: Name each character's need, and give each one a concrete give-away the other can answer, such as Brick holding through his pause or Reuben being exact with her.

plan.pair.why: The collision only works between these two: Brick's numbered audits measure Reuben and find him tiny, and his early exits convince her she has crushed him. The setups pair their two posture contraptions and their two mirror rehearsals, and the opening heat is a geometry duel between his short left-hook and her veined length. Some of the click logic, dropping the list and staying past the punchline, is close to a generic armour-drop.
evidence: Brick's numbered audits make Reuben feel measured and found tiny; Reuben's preemptive exits make Brick feel she has already crushed him
plan.pair.raise: Make the click turn on something only this pair could do, such as Reuben auditing Brick's geometry back at her and coming out kind.

plan.knowledge.why: Private material reaches the chat by explicit routes. The pasted rehearsal note and the pasted checklist carry the lentils and the rosé box, and the setups move from 'planted' to 'admits' before anyone uses them. The opening geometry banter relies only on profile body data. It is not higher because the plan doesn't track who knows what at each stage, for instance when Reuben learns about the interview behind Brick's 'strategic pause'.

plan.events.why: The plan schedules no events from the outside world. No dive-bar regular, indie singer, hotel or interviewer presses in during the night. Every complication is self-generated: the two pasted notes and the two snaps. The brief supplies named people and places that could intrude, such as the misidentified regular and the revolving-door hotel, but they stay in the origin backstory and never act tonight.

plan.setups.why: All three setups have a plant, a middle return and an end beat, and the click ending pays them as a trade of contraptions and a skipped rehearsal. The fall-apart ending pays only the posture and door setups ('fake posture and broken doors'), so the mirror-rehearsal setup has no failure payoff. Setup 2's end is an abstract theme ('fear of not fitting') rather than a beat. That keeps it from a 5, while the full plant-to-payoff chains keep it above the line.

plan.endings.why: The click ending has Brick abandoning her lists to invite him over and Reuben staying past his exit reflex, which pays the setups as a trade. The fall-apart ending has both snaps firing, with a final audit and a pre-emptive bow-out. These are different directions, not one scene with a swapped last line. Both are sketched mainly as quoted closing lines, and the collapse is simply both defences triggering on schedule, so neither is yet the best version of its outcome.
evidence: Brick drops the list (`No numbers. Come over.`); Reuben stays past the punchline (`I am not leaving early 🙂`)

Brick uses a lowercase 'hm.', numbered lists and two-word verdicts. Most single lines can be attributed without names ('hm. Unlikely.' against 'I have already lost this round, frankly.'). Some overlap remains, since both avoid contractions and both speak as if interest is settled, so a plain declarative from either could blur.

The contraption trade is a charming button but not an unpredicted turn.

plan.collision.why: Both directions are named and fit both profiles: Brick's numbered audits press on Reuben's fear of being "physically negligible," and his preemptive exits feed her fear of being "too big and loud to fit anyone's life without breaking something." But the collision is only described in one sentence. No turn is planned where a specific audit makes him bolt, or where a specific exit lands on her as proof she broke something. Her snap trigger ("mocked as 'too much'") doesn't match the collision's mechanism (his exits), and the fall-apart line "You want an audience" doesn't answer his leaving, so the ending doesn't clearly turn on either direction.
evidence: Brick's numbered audits make Reuben feel measured and found tiny; Reuben's preemptive exits make Brick feel she has already crushed him.

plan.collision.raise: Plan one concrete beat per direction: for example, Brick numbering his proportions back at him ("1. Short. 2. Thick.") prompts "I shall see myself out," and that exit makes Brick say she has flattened him. Then tie the fall-apart lines to those beats.
